Senses.Explanation: This is a shout delivered immediately as the next move in a public interview, not a name for a special kind of cry. Teaching masters and other participants both perform it, and the next turn may answer, question, or evaluate the shout. Linji Yixuan shouts when an unnamed participant hesitates and then follows with a strike; another preserved Linji encounter has him shout first, receive a returning shout and bow, and strike. Muzhou Daoming tells an unnamed participant that he has received the participant's shout, then asks what comes after three or four shouts. In the Recorded Sayings of Rain Mountain, an unnamed participant shouts after Yushan Shangsi strikes, and Yushan covers his ears. Yangshan Huiji raises the whisk; the unnamed participant immediately shouts, and Yangshan grants that there was a shout but asks where Yangshan's fault lay. Shangquan Heshang shouts after a bow, Mengxi Heshang shouts at an arrival, Zhihai Benyi shouts at hesitation, and Weiji Zhi shouts during her exchange with her teacher. Across these turns, the first graph supplies immediate narrative sequence and the second supplies the audible action; actor, trigger, reply, and a following blow do not create different things.
Senses.Note: The exact phrase occurs 4,723 times in 345 allowed texts. Across the concordance, resident-teacher subjects occur 1,463 times in 215 texts and participant subjects 1,161 times in 194 texts, so the construction is not exclusive to the teaching-seat speaker. Longer forms add a result, direct speech, or a counted single shout; they remain family constructions rather than new senses of the two-graph phrase. The corresponding entries for shout, a single shout, then struck, and hesitation carry their own definitions and are not copied into this one.

Occurrences.Kwic: 三度被打僧擬議師便喝隨後打
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Old Recorded Sayings of Venerable Masters (古尊宿語錄), in the explicitly headed Linji Yixuan section. Linji recounts his three questions and blows under Huangbo Xiyun; when the current unnamed participant hesitates over Linji's account, Linji is the exact shouter and then strikes. Huangbo belongs to the recounted history, not the stored headword turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 僧便喝。師曰。老僧被你一喝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元), in the explicitly headed Muzhou Daoming section. An unnamed monk is the exact shouter; Muzhou Daoming answers that he has received the monk's one shout and continues the exchange. The line, expanded unit, section, title, TEI header, and parallel recension leave the non-master participant unnamed.

Recorded Sayings of Yushan Heshang (雨山和尚語錄), in Yushan Shangsi's own ascent-to-the-seat exchange. An unnamed monk is the exact shouter after Yushan strikes; Yushan then covers his ears. The complete unit, title and author statement name Yushan but not the non-master questioner, and no named parallel passage was found.

Strict Unification of the Five Lamps, fascicles 10–25 (五燈嚴統(第10卷-第25卷)), in the explicitly headed section for Shangquan Heshang of Jingmen. The complete exchange keeps Shangquan as the subject marked ‘master’; Shangquan Heshang is the exact shouter after the unnamed monk bows.

Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元), in the explicitly headed Mengxi Heshang section. The narrated arrival introduces an unnamed monk, while ‘the master’ remains the section owner; Mengxi Heshang is the exact actor who immediately shouts.

Occurrences.Kwic: 還我鏡來。僧擬議，師便喝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in the explicitly headed section for Zhihai Benyi of the eastern capital. Zhihai asks for the mirror back; when the unnamed monk hesitates, Zhihai Benyi is the exact shouter.

Occurrences.Kwic: 臨濟陞堂有僧出師便喝僧亦喝便禮拜師便打
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Comprehensive Collection of the Chan School's Linked Pearls of Verse on Old Cases (禪宗頌古聯珠通集) explicitly opens this raised case with Linji Yixuan ascending the hall. Linji is the exact first shouter; the unnamed monk returns a shout and bows, and Linji strikes. Later substitute comments by Yunmen Wenyan and Dajue are outside the stored headword turn.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師見僧來豎拂子其僧便喝師曰喝即不無且道老僧過在什麼處
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The surviving fascicles of the Jade-Flower Collection of the Transmission of the Lamp (傳燈玉英集（殘卷）), in the explicitly listed and headed Yangshan Huiji biography. An unnamed monk is the exact shouter after Yangshan raises the whisk; Yangshan grants that there was a shout and asks the monk to state Yangshan's fault. The complete biography and all six attribution rungs do not name the non-master participant.

Occurrences.Kwic: 師曰：甜瓜徹蒂甜，苦瓜連根苦。雲曰：你又恁麼去也。師便喝。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: The Complete Book of the Five Lamps, fascicles 34–120 (五燈全書(第34卷-第120卷)), in the explicitly headed biography of the nun Weiji Zhi of Xiongsheng in Hangzhou. Within the complete teacher-student exchange, ‘Yun’ marks Shiqi Tongyun and ‘the master’ marks the section subject; Weiji Zhi is the exact shouter after her teacher's reply.

Occurrences.Kwic: 頭問。那箇是汝心。師曰。見言語者是。頭便喝出。
Occurrences.AttributionNote: Five Lamps Compendium (五燈會元), in Dadian Baotong's explicitly headed biography, names Shitou Xiqian inline as ‘Shitou’ before this question. Shitou is the exact actor who shouts Dadian out. The added result complement makes this the longer family construction ‘then shouted him out’; it tests the boundary but does not buy depth for the two-graph headword.
